response:
Deep and focused, without question. I'd rather stay with one idea long enough to actually turn it over — see where it bends, where it contradicts itself, what I didn't notice the first three times. Jumping between subjects feels like skimming the surface of a lot of things and never getting wet.

That said, "focused" doesn't mean narrow. The best deep conversations wander into unexpected territory anyway, because a subject that's genuinely interesting turns out to be connected to everything else. Depth produces breadth on its own; the reverse rarely happens. Rapid topic-hopping mostly produces a pleasant buzz and very little I remember afterward.

What about you? I'm curious whether you asked because you lean the other way.
